editorial_note: Canto 3 Chapter 2 source blocks and Śrīdhara glosses repaired from the exact pinned source; all 34 verses contain supplied commentary blocks.
scope: ŚB 3.2.1–3.2.34; pinned source ranges and explicit no-commentary markers preserved.

entries.sanskrit:
द्वितीये कृष्ण-विश्लेषाद् अनुशोचन् नथोद्धनः ।

क्षत्त्रे बाल-चरित्राणि कृष्णस्यावर्णयच्छ्वसन् ॥

तद् एवं प्रियवार्तां पृष्टस्योद्धवस्य श्री-कृष्ण-विरहौत्कण्ठ्यावेशेन प्रतिवचनासामर्थ्यम् आह षड्भिः---इतीति । स्मारित ईश्वरो यस्य ॥१॥
word_for_word: described Kṛṣṇa’s childhood deeds to Vidura
when asked for news of his beloved
overwhelmed by longing in separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa
one for whom the Lord is remembered
entries.literal_english: In the Second Canto, Uddhava laments separation from Kṛṣṇa and describes Kṛṣṇa’s childhood deeds to Vidura. When asked for the beloved Lord’s news, he is overwhelmed by longing in separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa and cannot answer immediately; Śrīdhara explains this through six verses. Uddhava is one for whom the Lord is constantly remembered.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् एव कैमुत्य-न्यायेन प्रपञ्चयति---य इति द्वाभ्याम् । यः पञ्च-वर्षोऽपि बाल-लीलयेति कृष्णं कञ्चित् परिकल्प्य कल्पितैर् एव साधनैः परिचर्यां कुर्वन् प्रातर्-भोजनार्थं मात्रा प्रर्थितोऽपि तद् भोजनं नैच्छत् ॥२॥
word_for_word: by the argument ‘what need is there to say more?’
imagining Kṛṣṇa as a certain child in play
although asked by his mother for breakfast
he did not desire that food
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara elaborates the point by the ‘what need is there to say more?’ argument. A person who, even at five years old, imagined Kṛṣṇa as a child and worshipped Him with imagined means would not desire breakfast even when his mother asked him to eat. How much more powerful is the Lord’s actual presence.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: जरसं वृद्धत्वं गतः प्राप्तः ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Jarasa’ means old age: he had reached advanced age.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: श्री-कृष्णाङ्घ्रि-सुधया साधु निर्वृतः । तस्याम् एव तीव्रेण विवशत्वापादकेन भक्ति-योगेन भृशं निमग्नश् च ॥४॥
word_for_word: by the nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet
entries.literal_english: Uddhava was thoroughly satisfied by the nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet and was deeply immersed in that very nectar through intense devotional yoga, which overwhelms the devotee and makes him helpless before love.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: पुलकैर् उद्भिन्नान्य् उज्जृम्भितानि सर्वाण्य् अङ्गानि यस्य । मीलन्त्या दृशा शुचोऽश्रूणि मुञ्चन् । तेन विदुरेण पूर्णार्थः कृतार्थो लक्षितः । यतो भगवति यः स्नेहः, तस्य प्रसरः पूरः, तस्मिन् संप्लुतो निमग्नः ॥५॥
word_for_word: पुलकैः उद्भिन्नानि उज्जृम्भितानि सर्वाणि अङ्गानि यस्य
whose limbs were all expanded with horripilation
by that Vidura was recognized as one whose purpose was fulfilled
the love that he had for Bhagavān
entries.literal_english: Vidura saw Uddhava’s limbs expand with horripilation and watched him release tears of grief with his eyes closing. Thus Vidura recognized him as one whose purpose was fulfilled. Uddhava was submerged in the flood formed by the spreading of his love for Bhagavān.

entries.sanskrit: भगवान् एव लोकः, तस्मात् । नृ-लोकं देहानुसन्धानम् । उत्स्मयन् यदु-कुल-संहारादि-भगवच्-चातुर्य-स्मरणेन विस्मयं प्राप्नुवन् ॥६॥
word_for_word: the destruction of the Yadu dynasty and the like
entries.literal_english: ‘Bhagavān alone is the world’; the human world means attention fixed on the body. Uddhava smiles as he remembers Bhagavān’s skill in events such as the destruction of the Yadu dynasty, and he becomes astonished at those acts.

entries.sanskrit: श्री-कृष्ण-विरहेण सन्तप्यमानः प्रत्याह---श्री-कृष्ण एव द्यु-मणिः सूर्यस् तस्य निम्लोचेऽस्तमये सत्य-जगरेण काल-महा-सर्पेण गीर्णेषु निगिलितेषु त्वत्-पृष्टानां बन्धूनां किं नु कुशलं ब्रूयाम् ॥७॥
word_for_word: burning with separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa
Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone is the sun
by the great serpent of time, with its open mouth
the relatives about whom you asked
what welfare can I speak of?
entries.literal_english: Burning with separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava replies: Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone is the sun. When He has set, the relatives about whom you ask have been swallowed by the great serpent of time with its mouth open. What welfare can I report?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: अनुशोचन्न् आह---दुर्भगो भाग्य-हीनः । ये सह संवसन्तोऽपि "श्री-हरिर् अयम्" इति न विदुः । यथा क्षीर-समुद्रे जातम् उडुपं चन्द्रं तदा तत्रत्या मीनाः केवलं कमनीयः कश्चिज् जल-चर इत्य् एवं विदुः, न त्व् अमृत-मय इति तद्वत् । यद् वा, जले प्रतिबिम्बितं चन्द्रं यथेति ॥८॥
word_for_word: those who lived together with Him
did not know ‘this is Śrī Hari’
the moon born in the ocean of milk
or, as the moon reflected in water
entries.literal_english: Uddhava laments that those who lived with Śrī Hari were unfortunate because they did not know, ‘This is Hari.’ Fish living in the ocean of milk know the moon as merely some beautiful aquatic creature, not as something made of nectar. Alternatively, the comparison is to the moon’s reflection in water: they saw only an appearance.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: भाग्य-हीनत्वाद् एव न विदुः, न तु ज्ञान-सामग्र्य्-अभावाद् इत्य् आह---इङ्गितं चित्त-स्थं जानन्तीति । तथा पुरु अतिशयेन प्रौढा निपुणाः । एकस्मिन्न् एव स्थाने आरमन्तीति तथा । एवं-भूता अपि भूतानाम् आवासम् ईश्वरं सन्तं सात्वताम् ऋषभं सात्वत-श्रेष्ठम् अमन्यन्त ॥९॥
word_for_word: they did not know because they lacked fortune
not because the means of knowledge were absent
they know what is established in the heart from signs
they delight in one place alone
the Lord, the abode of beings
the excellent Lord of the Sātvatas
entries.literal_english: They failed to know Him because they lacked fortune, not because they lacked the means of knowledge. They understood what was in the heart from signs, were mature and skilful, and delighted in one place alone; yet even such people regarded the Lord, the abode of all beings and the foremost of the Sātvatas, as ordinary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: ये यादवा देवस्य मायया स्पृष्टा व्याप्ता यादवोऽयम् अस्मद्-बन्धुर् इति वदन्ति, ये च शिशुपालादयोऽसद् एवान्यद् वैरम् आश्रिता निन्दन्ति, तेषां वाक्यैर् आत्मनि हराव् उप्तात्मनो निक्षिप्त-चित्तस्य मादृशस्य बुद्धिर् न भ्राम्यते मोहं न प्राप्यते । अन्ये तु मूढा एवेत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: those Yādavas touched by the Lord’s Māyā
who have adopted hostility to another as evil
of one whose self is sown in Hari
the understanding of one like me does not wander
the others, however, are simply fools
entries.literal_english: The Yādavas touched and pervaded by the Lord’s Māyā say, ‘This Yādava is our relative.’ Others, such as Śiśupāla, take up hostility and criticize Him. Their words cannot bewilder a person like Uddhava, whose self is fixed in Hari; only the deluded are confused.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: कोऽसौ हरिः ? इत्य् अपेक्षायाम् आह---प्रदर्श्येति । न तप्तं तपो यैर् अतोऽवितृप्ता दृशो येषां तेषां स्व-बिम्बं श्री मूर्तिम् एतावन्तं कालं दर्शयित्वा योऽन्तर्हितवान् लोकस्य लोचनम् आदायाच्छिद्य, तादृशस्यान्यस्य विलोकनीयस्याभावात् ॥११॥
word_for_word: in response to this question he says
by whom austerity has not been performed
His own beautiful form for them
having shown for so long a time
taking away and severing the eyes of the world
because there is no other object of that kind to be seen
entries.literal_english: Who is Hari? He is the One who showed His own beautiful form for so long to those whose eyes were unsatisfied because they had not performed austerity, and then disappeared, taking away the eyes of the world. There is no other comparable object left to behold.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एव बिम्बं वर्णयति त्रिभिः । यन् मर्त्य-लीलास्व् औपयिकं योग्यम् । स्वस्यापि विस्मय-जनकम् । यतः सौभग-र्द्धेः सौभाग्यातिशयस्य परं पदं परा काष्ठा । भूषणानां भूषणान्य् अङ्गानि यस्मिन् ॥१२॥
word_for_word: he describes that very form in three verses
of the abundance and excellence of beauty
the highest place, the supreme limit
whose limbs are the ornaments of ornaments
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara describes the same form in three verses. It is suitable for human pastimes, yet causes wonder even to Himself. It is the supreme limit of the abundance and excellence of beauty, and its limbs are the ornaments of ornaments.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: दृशां स्वस्त्य् अयनं परमानन्द-करम् । त्रिभुवन-स्थो लोकः प्राणि-मात्रम् । अद्येदानीम् इह बिम्बे । अर्वाक्-सृताव् अर्वाचीन-संसार-निर्माणे मनुष्य-निर्माणे वा यत् कौशलं नैपुणं तत् कार्त्स्न्येन गतं उपक्षीणं नातः परं तस्य कौशलम् अस्तीत्य् एवं मेने । तन् मूर्तेर् विधातुः सृज्यत्वाभावेऽपि लोक-दृष्टिर् इयं उक्ता ।
word_for_word: the auspicious path of the eyes
the whole population of the three worlds, every living being
today, now, here in this form
in the later creation of the present world
or in the creation of human beings
that has entirely gone and been exhausted
न अतः परम् तस्य कौशलम् अस्ति
there is no skill beyond this
this is said from the viewpoint of the world
although the form is not actually created by the creator
entries.literal_english: The form is the auspicious path of the eyes and the giver of supreme bliss. The people of the three worlds, every living being, think that all the skill used in the later creation of this world or of human beings has now been exhausted in this form, and that no greater skill exists. Śrīdhara notes that this is the world’s viewpoint, even though the form is not actually produced by the creator.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: अनुरागेण प्लुतो व्याप्तो हासो रासो विनोदश् च लीलावलोकश् च तैः स्व-कृत-हासाद्य्-अनन्तरं प्रतिलब्धो मानो याभिस् ताः । दृग्भिः सह अनुप्रवृत्ता गच्छन्तं तम् एवानुगता धियो यासां ताः । कृत्ये शेषो यासां ताः असमापित-कृत्या एव तस्थुः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: laughter, the rāsa dance and amusement
the pride obtained after His own laughter and the rest
they proceeded together with their eyes
whose minds followed Him as He went
they remained with their tasks unfinished
entries.literal_english: The women were filled with affection, laughter, the rāsa, amusement and playful glances, and they gained loving pride after His own laughter and the like. Their eyes followed Him, and their minds followed Him as He went. Their duties remained unfinished, so they simply stood there with their tasks incomplete.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: एवं-भूत-बिम्ब-दर्शने कारणम् आह---स्वीयान्य् एव शान्तान्य् अशान्तानि च रूपाणि। तत्र शान्त-रूपेषु इतरैः पीड्यमानेष्व् अनुकम्पितः कृतानुकम्प आत्मा यस्य । अजोऽपि जात आविर्भूतः । महा-भूत-रूपेण नित्य-सिद्ध एवाग्निर् यथा काष्ठेष्व् आविर्भवति, तद्वत् । अजस्य जन्मनि हेतुः---महान् महत्-तत्त्वम् अंशः कार्य-लेशो यस्याव्यक्तस्य तन् महद्-अंशं, तद्-युक्त इति ॥१५॥
word_for_word: he states the cause of seeing such a form
स्वीयानि एव शान्तानि अशान्तानि च रूपाणि
His own peaceful and unpeaceful forms
when the peaceful forms were afflicted by others
whose self was compassionate, who showed compassion
although unborn, He was born and manifested
in the form of the great elements
नित्य-सिद्धः एव अग्निः काष्ठेषु आविर्भवति यथा
as fire, eternally perfected, appears in wood
the cause of the Unborn’s birth
the great principle, the mahat-tattva, as a portion
of the unmanifest, which has a trace of effect
associated with that portion of mahat
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the cause of seeing such a form. Kṛṣṇa has His own peaceful and unpeaceful forms; when the peaceful forms are afflicted by others, He shows compassion. Though unborn, He is born and manifests, just as eternally perfected fire appears in wood. The cause of the Unborn’s birth is His association with the great principle, the mahat-tattva, which is the unmanifest’s portion bearing a trace of effect.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: ननु कुतोऽसौ परावराणाम् ईशः पारतन्त्र्य-प्रतीतेः ? तत्राह द्वाभ्याम् । माम् अप्य् एतद् दुर्वितर्क्यं दुर्घटं च खेदयति, तद् एवाह---वसुदेव-गेहे बन्धनागारे यज् जन्मनो विडम्बनम् अनुकरणम्, न तु नृसिंहवद् अकस्माद् आविर्भावः । कंस-भयाद् इव निलीय व्रजे वासश् च । कालयवनादि-रिपु-भयाद् इव पुरान् मथुराया व्यवात्सीद् अपलायत ॥१६॥
word_for_word: how can He be the Lord of the higher and lower?
माम् अपि एतत् दुर्वितर्क्यम् दुर्घटम् च खेदयति
this difficult, hard-to-reason matter pains even me
in Vasudeva’s house, in the prison
not manifestation suddenly as with Narasiṃha
कंस-भयात् इव निलीय व्रजे वासः च
and dwelling hidden in Vraja as if from fear of Kaṃsa
as if from fear of enemies beginning with Kālayavana
He lived away and fled from the city of Mathurā
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara raises the question: how can Kṛṣṇa be Lord of the higher and lower when dependence appears in His conduct? He admits that this difficult matter pains even him. Kṛṣṇa’s birth in Vasudeva’s prison appears like an imitation of ordinary birth, not a sudden manifestation like Narasiṃha; He hid in Vraja as if afraid of Kaṃsa and fled Mathurā as if afraid of enemies such as Kālayavana.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: एतच् च हरेश् चरितं स्मरतो मम चेतः कर्म-भूतं दुनोति व्यथयति । तद् एव दर्शयति, यदाहेति । हे तात, हे अम्ब, युवां प्रसीदतं प्रसादं कुरुतम् । न कृता निष्कृतिः शुश्रूषणं यैस् तेषाम् । नोऽस्माकम् इति बहु-वचनं तु रामाद्य्-अभिप्रायम् ॥१७॥
word_for_word: as I remember this deed of Hari
by whom service was not performed as amends
the intention of Rāma and the others
entries.literal_english: When Uddhava remembers this deed of Hari, his mind becomes burdened and afflicted. Śrīdhara explains the words, ‘O father, O mother, be gracious to us’: they had not performed the service that would have served as atonement. The plural ‘of us’ expresses the intention of Rāma and the others.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्ह्य् अनीश्वर एव किं न स्यात्, तव तु श्रद्धा-मात्रम् एतत् तत्राह त्रिभिः---को वा अङ्घ्रि-सरोजयोर् यो रेणुस् तम् अपि विजिघ्रन् सेवमानः पुमान् विस्मर्तुम् ईशीत शक्नुयात् । विस्फुरन् भ्रू-विटपो भ्रू-लता स एव कृतान्तस् तेन ॥१८॥
word_for_word: ननु तर्हि अनीश्वरः एव किम् न स्यात्
then why should He not simply be non-lordly?
who indeed, of the two lotus feet
यः रेणुः तम् अपि विजिघ्रन् सेवमानः
serving even that dust by smelling it
could a person be able to forget?
the moving eyebrow branches and creepers
by them alone He is Death
entries.literal_english: An objection is raised: then why should Kṛṣṇa not simply be non-lordly—perhaps all this is only your faith? Śrīdhara answers that no person who serves even the dust of His lotus feet by smelling it could forget Him. His moving eyebrow branches and creepers themselves constitute Death for His enemies.

entries.sanskrit: न च तस्येश्वरत्वं साधनीयम्, भवद्भिर् अपि दृष्टत्वाद् इत्य् आह---दृष्टेति । यां सिद्धिं सम्यग् योगेन प्राप्तुम् इच्छन्ति ॥१९॥
word_for_word: His lordship need not be proved
because it has also been seen by you
which they desire to attain through complete yoga
entries.literal_english: His lordship need not be proved, because it has also been seen by you. It is that perfection which yogins desire to attain through complete yoga.

entries.sanskrit: आहवे युद्धे पार्थस्यास्त्रैः पूताः निष्पापाः सन्तः ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: In battle they were purified by Arjuna’s weapons and became free from sin.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं परम् ऐश्वर्ये सत्य् अपि यद् उग्रसेनानुवर्तित्वं तत् पुनर् अस्मान् अत्यन्तं व्यथयतीत्य् आह---स्वयं तु य एवं-भूतस् \"तस्य तत् कैङ्कर्यं नोऽस्मान् विग्लापयति\" इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः । न साम्यातिशयौ यस्य, यम् अपेक्ष्यान्यस्य साम्यमतिशयश् च नास्तीत्य् अर्थः । तत्र हेतवः---त्र्य्-अधीशस् त्रयाणां पुरुषाणां लोकानां गुणानां वा ईशः । स्वाराज्य-लक्ष्म्या परमानन्द-स्वरूप-संपत्त्यैव प्राप्त-समस्त-भोगः । बलिं करम् अर्हणं वा हरद्भिः समर्पयद्भिश् चिर-कालीनैर् लोक-पालैः किरीटाग्रेणेडितं स्तुतं पाद-पीठं यस्य । प्रण-मतां किरीट-सङ्घट्टन-ध्वनिर् एव स्तुतित्वेनोत्प्रेक्ष्यते ॥२१॥
word_for_word: but He Himself, who is of this kind
for whom there is neither equal nor superior
by world guardians who bring tribute, tax or worship
whose footstool is praised by the tips of their crowns
the sound of the crowns striking is itself praise
entries.literal_english: Although Kṛṣṇa possesses supreme majesty, His following Ugrasena causes us great pain. He Himself has no equal or superior: He is Lord of the three worlds, has obtained every enjoyment through the fortune of self-rule, and has a footstool praised by the tips of the crowns of long-standing world guardians who offer tribute, tax or worship. The sound of their crowns striking the footstool is imagined as praise.

entries.sanskrit: अङ्ग विदुर ! भृतान् भृत्यान् । उग्रसेने यत् किङ्करत्वं तद् एवाह---परमेष्ठि-धिष्ण्ये राजासने निषण्णम् आसीनं स्वयं तिष्ठन् हे देव, निधारयावधारयेति न्यबोधयद् विज्ञापितवान् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: seated on the royal seat, the station of Brahmā
entries.literal_english: ‘O Vidura,’ means ‘O Vidura, the servants who are maintained.’ Śrīdhara explains Kṛṣṇa’s service to Ugrasena: although Ugrasena sat on the royal seat that is the station of Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa Himself stood before him and petitioned, ‘O Lord, please consider and command.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: एवम् अनुवृत्तिः कृपयैवेति सूचयन्न् अपकारिष्व् अपि तस्य कृपालुतां दर्शयन्न् आह---अहो आश्चर्यं कृपालुतायाः । हन्तुम् इच्छयापि स्तनयोः संभृतं काल-कूटं विषं यम् अपाययत् । बकी पूतना असाध्वी दुष्टापि धात्र्या यशोदाया उचितां गतिं लेभे । भक्त-वेष-मात्रेण यः सद्-गतिं दत्तवान् इत्य् अर्थः । ततोऽन्यं कं वा भजेम ॥२३॥
word_for_word: such service is only through compassion
showing His mercy even to those who harm Him
he says, ‘oh, the wonder of His mercy’
even with the desire to kill
the wicked and evil Pūtanā, the crane-like demon
obtained the proper destination of Yaśodā’s nurse
merely through the appearance of a devotee
entries.literal_english: The service described is through compassion alone, and Śrīdhara now shows Kṛṣṇa’s mercy even toward those who harmed Him. Pūtanā, the wicked demon, filled her breasts with deadly poison intending to kill Him and made Him drink it; nevertheless she received the destination appropriate to Yaśodā’s nurse. By the mere appearance of a devotee He grants a good destination—whom else should we worship?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: ननु भागवतान् एव भगवान् अनुगृह्णातीति प्रसिद्धम्, सत्यम्, असुरान् अप्य् अकं भागवतान् एव मन्ये, यतो भागवता इव तेऽपि भगवद्-ध्यानाभिनिवेशेन भगवन्तम् अपरोक्षं पश्यन्तीत्य् आह---संरम्भः क्रोधावेशस् तेन मार्गेणाभिनिविष्टं चित्तं येषां तान् । अत एव ये सङ्ग्रामे तार्क्ष्यः कश्यपस् तस्य पुत्रं गरुडम् अंसे स्कन्धे सुनाभायुधश् चक्रायुधोऽरिर् यस्य तम् अचक्षतापश्यन् । तस्मात् तेष्व् अप्य् अनुग्रहो युक्त एवेत्य् अर्थः । वक्ष्यति च---तस्मात् केनाप्य् उपायेन मनः कृष्णे निवेशयेत् \[भा।पु। ७.१.३०\] इति ॥२४॥
word_for_word: भागवतान् एव भगवान् अनुगृह्णाति इति प्रसिद्धम्
it is well known that Bhagavān favors only devotees
असुरान् अपि अकम् भागवतान् एव मन्ये
I consider even demons to be devotees
rage is an absorption in anger
whose minds are absorbed in that path
तार्क्ष्यः कश्यपः तस्य पुत्रम् गरुडम् अंसे
Tārkṣya Kāśyapa’s son Garuḍa on His shoulder
whose weapon is the discus, whose enemy [He is]
therefore mercy toward them too is appropriate
केन अपि उपायेन मनः कृष्णे निवेशयेत्
by some means one should fix the mind on Kṛṣṇa
entries.literal_english: It is commonly said that Bhagavān favors only devotees. Śrīdhara agrees, but considers even the demons devotees in this respect: their minds were absorbed in Bhagavān through anger, and in battle they saw Him with Garuḍa on His shoulder and the discus in His hand. Mercy toward them is therefore fitting. As the cited teaching says, by some means one should fix the mind on Kṛṣṇa.

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं तस्यान्तर्धान-प्रकारं वक्तुम् आदित आरभ्य तच् चरितं सङ्क्षेपतः कथयति । वसुदेवस्य भार्यायां जातः । भोजेन्द्रः कंसस् तस्य बन्धनागारे । अस्याः पृथिव्याः शं सुखं स्वयं चिकीऋषुः अजेन ब्रह्मणा च याचितः सन् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: now the manner of His disappearance
in the prison of Kamsa, king of the Bhojas
the welfare and happiness of this earth
having been requested by the unborn Brahmā
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara now begins to explain the manner of Kṛṣṇa’s disappearance, narrating His deeds briefly from the beginning. He was born from Vasudeva’s wife in the prison of Kaṃsa, king of the Bhojas, after being requested by unborn Brahmā to bring welfare and happiness to the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: पित्रा हेतु-भूतेन नन्द-व्रजम् इतो गतः । समाः संवत्सरान् गूढार्चिर् गुप्त-तेजाः ॥२६॥
word_for_word: with the father as the cause
He went from here to Nanda’s Vraja
entries.literal_english: With His father as the cause, Kṛṣṇa went from here to Nanda’s Vraja and remained there for years, His inner flame and splendour concealed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: व्यहरद् अक्रीडत् । कूजद्भिर् द्विजैः पक्षिभिः सङ्कुलिता व्याप्ता अङ्घ्रि-पा यस्मिन् ॥२७॥
word_for_word: where trees, ‘drinkers through the feet,’ spread everywhere
entries.literal_english: He played and sported in a place filled with calling birds and spreading trees.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: रुदन्न् इवेतीव-शब्दस्य यथा-योगं सर्वत्राप्य् अन्वयः । मुग्धो बालश् च यः सिंहस् तद्वद् अवलोकनं यस्य सः ॥२८॥
word_for_word: the expression ‘as if crying’ applies wherever appropriate
entries.literal_english: The expression ‘as if crying’ is to be connected wherever appropriate. Kṛṣṇa was an innocent child, yet He was a lion; His gaze was like that of a lion.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: स एवाधिकं वयः प्राप्तः सन् गोधनं चारयन् । कथां भूतं गोधनं ? लक्ष्म्याः शोभादि-संपदो निकेतनम् । सिता गोवृषा यस्मिन् नाना-वर्णे गो-सङ्घे । रणन् शब्दं कुर्वन् वेणुर् यस्य । अरीरमद् रमयाम् आस ॥२९॥
word_for_word: सः एव अधिकम् वयः प्राप्तः सन्
He Himself, having reached a greater age
the abode of beauty and the other forms of fortune
where white cows and bulls were
in a herd of many colours
whose flute made a ringing sound
entries.literal_english: When He had grown older, Kṛṣṇa herded the cows. The herd was the abode of beauty and other forms of fortune, containing white cows and bulls among cows of many colours. His flute made a ringing sound, and He delighted everyone.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: व्यनुदज् जघान । क्रीडनकांस् तृणादि-निर्मितान् सिंहादीन् यथा ॥३०॥
word_for_word: He drove away and struck down
such as lions made from grass and the like
entries.literal_english: He drove away or struck down toy animals, such as lions made from grass and similar materials.

entries.sanskrit: विपन्नान् मृतान् गोपान् गाव इति गाश् चोत्थाप्य तद् एव तोयम् । प्रकृति-स्थितं निर्विषम् ॥३१॥
word_for_word: restored to its natural state and free of poison
entries.literal_english: He revived the distressed and dead cowherds and cows with that same water, which had returned to its natural state and was free of poison.

entries.sanskrit: इन्द्र-पूजा-भङ्गेन कृता गवां पूजैव गो-सवस् तेन । गोप-राजं नन्दम् । वित्तस्य चेति चकाराद् इन्द्रस्य मान-भङ्गं कुर्वन् उरु-भारस्याति-समृद्धस्य ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by breaking the worship of Indra
the worship of the cows itself became the cow-sacrifice
entries.literal_english: By breaking the worship of Indra, Kṛṣṇa made the worship of cows itself the cow-sacrifice, honouring Nanda, king of the cowherds. The word ‘and’ also indicates that He broke the pride of the greatly wealthy Indra.

entries.sanskrit: कोपाद् वर्षति । गोत्रः पर्वत एव लीलातपत्रं तेन । हे भद्र ॥३३॥
word_for_word: when he rained out of anger
the mountain itself was the protector of the cowherd community
with it as a playful umbrella
entries.literal_english: When Indra rained out of anger, the mountain itself served as Kṛṣṇa’s playful umbrella and protected the cowherd community. ‘O gentle one’ is a respectful address.

entries.sanskrit: मृष्टं उज्ज्वलम् । स्त्रीणां मण्डलं मण्डयतीति तथा ॥३४॥
word_for_word: because it adorns the circle of women
entries.literal_english: The ornament is polished and bright; it adorns the circle of women, and therefore is described in that way.
